approvalBasis: The independent NewsStand review dated 2026-07-25 found the material claims entailed by the three cited sources. This record does not approve deployment.

truthExplanation.circulatingFraming: AI provenance labels and technical watermarks can be presented as if they prove that the labelled claim is true or the underlying system is compliant.
truthExplanation.whatHappened: Google announced that it signed the voluntary EU transparency code and connected that commitment with C2PA and SynthID provenance technologies.
truthExplanation.evidenceEstablishes: The records establish Google's announcement and the Commission's description of the code as voluntary and not conclusive proof of compliance.
truthExplanation.evidenceDoesNotEstablish: They do not establish that provenance metadata verifies factual truth, that every implementation is effective, or that signing the code proves legal compliance.
truthExplanation.mechanism: Provenance systems can carry information about origin or edit history; deciding whether the represented claim is true requires separate evidence and verification.
truthExplanation.realWorldImpact: A reader can use a label as useful source context while still checking the claim, date, scope and supporting evidence independently.
truthExplanation.uncertainty: Implementation quality, coverage, adoption and adversarial robustness vary and were not independently established by this source set.
truthExplanation.headlineRisk: Calling a label a truth detector would merge origin, authenticity, factual accuracy and legal compliance into one misleading signal.
truthExplanation.editorialDecision: Keep the label-versus-truth correction as the dominant lesson and attribute vendor and regulator claims separately from LAiDIES analysis.

aidbComparison.rationale: The available AIDB archive through July 25 contained no substantive analysis of this exact code-signing and provenance-label story; no AIDB interpretation or wording was used.

claims.claim: Google said it signed the EU AI Act Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content and connected that commitment to C2PA and SynthID.
claims.assessment: Entailed vendor announcement, labelled in the reader.

claims.claim: The European Commission describes the code as voluntary and says adherence is not conclusive evidence of compliance.
Provenance can support origin/edit-history checks but does not itself establish whether a claim is true.
claims.assessment: Clearly presented as LAiDIES analysis rather than a regulator quote.
